blocks.heading: Energy Conditions and Focusing
blocks.text: The Averaged Null Energy Condition (AANEC) provides a weaker constraint than pointwise energy conditions, which are systematically violated by quantum fields. However, AANEC alone is insufficient to guarantee the local or integrated focusing required for Penrose-type trapped-surface formation. An explicit averaged null-convergence condition must therefore be specified as an independent geometric hypothesis to drive the Raychaudhuri focusing equation. Without this explicit mathematical form, the transition from energy condition satisfaction to negative expansion scalar remains unverified.

blocks.heading: Compactness and Astrophysical Confounders
blocks.text: The Misner-Sharp compactness parameter is central to identifying the threshold for trapped-surface formation, yet its specific formal definition and the associated effective mass formula within the chosen metric class remain undefined. Furthermore, the operationalization of astrophysical confounders—including equation of state models, rotation, magnetic fields, and explosion energetics—lacks precise measurement specifications. These unresolved variables prevent the rigorous calculation of model-dependent thresholds and limit the ability to distinguish the formal theorem's predictions from alternative stellar-physics mechanisms.
